note: Every third-party file this node serves from /lib/, with its licence, its copyright holder and where its bytes came from. This is the MACHINE-READABLE source of truth; VENDORED.md is the same inventory written for a person, and the two are kept in sync by `pnpm check:licenses`. THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md is generated from this file plus the npm dependency tree by `pnpm gen:notices` — do not edit that file by hand. A `files` entry is a path relative to public/lib/, either an exact name or a `dir/**` prefix; the check refuses a served file that no component claims, which is what stops a new vendored library from arriving without its notice.

components.copyright: Copyright (c) The Processing Foundation and the p5.js contributors
components.note: WEAK COPYLEFT, and the one place on this node where that matters. p5 is served unmodified as its own file at a stable URL; nothing links it statically and nothing derives from it, so an app that calls p5 stays under its own licence. The LGPL asks for three things and all three are here: the licence text (LICENSES/p5.txt), the notice that the library is used and can be replaced, and the complete source of the exact version, which is the tarball in `sourceOffer`. Anyone may substitute their own p5 build by pointing their app at a different URL. Owner-approved 2026-07-16.

components.name: @ffmpeg/core (ffmpeg 5.1.4 compiled to WebAssembly)
components.sourceOffer: https://github.com/ffmpegwasm/ffmpeg.wasm (build scripts) and https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-5.1.4.tar.xz (the ffmpeg sources it was built from)
components.note: STRONG COPYLEFT, and the reason none of these three files is in git or in any AIMEAT package. The build enables libx264 and libx265, which makes the compiled result GPL-2.0-or-later; npm's `license: MIT` field describes the packaging and not the binary. All three files (the wasm and both emscripten loaders) are installed on the operator's own machine by `pnpm vendor:libs`, byte-identical to upstream and hash-pinned, so AIMEAT never distributes them and stays MIT. An operator who serves them is distributing GPL work under the GPL, and the source offer above is what that requires.

components.name: Preact
components.source: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/preact@10.29.8/dist/preact.mjs and hooks/dist/hooks.mjs — the package own ESM builds
components.note: Both files come from the SAME upstream dist. That is the whole requirement, and getting it wrong killed the app once: on 2026-08-31 preact was taken from one esm.sh build variant and hooks from another, the two ended up with different options objects, and the SPA died with AIMEAT failed to start. hooks/dist/hooks.mjs imports the bare specifier preact, which the importmap resolves to the same module the page uses; a build that imports ./preact.mjs relatively does NOT work here, because the importmap stamps a ?v= cache-busting query and the relative path does not carry it.
